title: Shawwal: keeping it going
hookLine: six fasts, and keeping Ramadan's habits
tomorrow: which ten days does a hadith say nothing beats for good deeds?

cards: The morning after Eid, the before-dawn alarm doesn't ring. The dates on the counter, the ones that broke every fast, have gone a little dry at the edges. The kitchen smells of leftover sweets instead of soup at sunset.
And there's a quiet question in the house: was that Ramadan person just visiting? Does the fasting simply stop? Not quite.
The next month, Shawwal, opens with an invitation.

teach.b: Shawwal is the month after Ramadan. It begins with Eid, and on Eid itself fasting is not allowed: the Prophet ﷺ forbade fasting on the two Eid days. Then comes the invitation, in Sahih Muslim.
Whoever fasts Ramadan and follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted for all time. Six days, not a second month.
Scholars differ on whether to keep them in a row right after Eid or spread them through Shawwal; the hadith just says six days of Shawwal.

But the six fasts point at something bigger: the habits shouldn't vanish with the moon. 'A'isha reports the Prophet saying that the deeds most beloved to God are the most constant, even if they're small.
Ramadan builds big things: the long nights, the full Qur'an, the hunger. Shawwal asks a smaller question.
Which one piece can you keep? A page a day instead of a juz'.
The dawn prayer, still on time. A date eaten slowly, with thanks. Small and steady beats big and gone.

how: After Eid al-Fitr many Muslims fast six voluntary days in Shawwal, some straight after Eid and some spread through the month, and try to keep one Ramadan habit, such as a daily portion of Qur'an.

games.q: your friend wants to keep something from Ramadan, but her schedule is packed. which plan fits Shawwal's lesson?
o: one long night of prayer each week, to make up for the month.
a few minutes of Qur'an every day: small, but kept.

games.why: the deeds most beloved to God are the most constant, even if small. a little every day keeps Ramadan going.

practice: Take a date, or a raisin, or any small piece of food. Eat it slowly: the first touch on the tongue, the sweetness, the chew, the swallow.
While the taste lasts, choose one Ramadan habit small enough to keep, and hold it in mind for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: Shawwal: the month after Ramadan. It opens with Eid, then invites six fasts, and a small habit kept.

orig.note: Arabic: the month after Ramadan, which opens with Eid al-Fitr.

carryVoice: Keep this one close: carry Ramadan forward, one small piece at a time. The month after counts too.
